name: Leaf salad
grown_as: A loose-leaf lettuce mix sown thickly and picked as young leaves, cut and come again (William's records: 'Lettuce mix', picked at 12 to 15 cm). No heart forms. Mixes hold frilly, oakleaf and smooth leaves in green and red; drawn as a mix of frilly green and red-edged leaves. ⚠️ CHECK the mix: some salad mixes also hold rocket, mustard or mizuna.
habit: Thick tufts of upright leaves 10 to 20 cm tall, each plant an open rosette with no heart. If left uncut the stem bolts to 60 to 90 cm.

leaf.arrangement: An open, upright rosette from a very short stem
leaf.type: Simple; in oakleaf kinds deeply lobed
leaf.outline: Oblong to obovate, 8 to 15 cm long when picked; oakleaf kinds cut into rounded lobes like an oak leaf
leaf.base: Narrowing into a broad, flat, pale midrib
leaf.margin: Frilled, crimped and wavy all round in Lollo kinds; smooth and wavy in others; no sharp teeth
leaf.veins: A pale midrib with branching side veins
leaf.surface: Soft, thin, hairless and slightly puckered
leaf.stalk: None, the base is the pale midrib
leaf.colour: A mix: fresh green leaves and green leaves flushed or edged with bronze-red

flower.form: A small head like a little dandelion, made only of strap-shaped florets, opening flat in the morning and closing by midday
flower.petals: No true petals to count: about 10 to 25 strap-shaped florets, each a single ray with five tiny teeth across its squared-off tip, laid out like the rays of a dandelion
flower.centre: No separate eye: the inner florets are shorter and the forked yellow styles stand up in the middle
flower.behind: A slim cylindrical cup (involucre) of narrow green bracts overlapping like roof tiles, longer than wide, sometimes tinged purple
flower.carried: Many heads on short stalks in a wide, branched, flat-topped spray at the top of a tall bolted stem, the heads facing up
flower.season: July to September, after the plant bolts

fruit: Each floret makes one seed (achene): slim, flattened, 3 to 4 mm, with fine lengthwise ribs, narrowing at the top into a thin beak carrying a tuft of soft white hairs (pappus). Seed colour is white-cream, grey, brown or black depending on variety. The heads open into small white fluffy clocks, much smaller and looser than a dandelion clock. The plant has milky sap.
seedling: Two smooth oval seed leaves, then oblong true leaves, sown thickly so the seedlings come up in a crowded row.

leaf: an oblong leaf narrowing into a pale midrib, no stalk
frilled or crimped wavy edge, no sharp teeth
bloom: a small pale yellow head of strap-shaped florets, like a little dandelion
a slim cup of overlapping green bracts behind
seed: slim, flat, ribbed seed 3 to 4 mm
young: an open upright tuft of loose leaves
crop: loose upright leaves 10 to 20 cm, frilly and some red-edged
cut leaves regrowing from the centre
flower: a tall branched stem with small clasping leaves
small pale yellow heads in a spray at the top
seedhead: small white fluffy clocks at the branch tips

look_alikes: Heading lettuce makes a firm heart. Rocket and mustard leaves in a mix are lobed and peppery. Prickly lettuce (Lactuca serriola) is the wild relative: a row of prickles under the midrib and leaves often turned edge-on to the sun. Endive and chicory have blue flowers and bitter leaves. Sow-thistles have spiny-edged, clasping leaves and larger yellow heads.
